phrases.translation: Kãf-Ha-Ya-’Aĩn- Ṣãd
phrases.explanation: These disconnected letters are recited at the opening of the surah. Commentators have reported different explanations for them, but no single expansion is established by the wording here. Their presence reminds the reader that revelation may include matters whose full meaning Allah knows, and the account that follows is part of that revealed message.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ a reminder of your Lord’s mercy to His servant Zachariah
phrases.explanation: The story is introduced as a reminder of Allah's mercy toward His servant Zachariah. Calling it a reminder directs readers to learn from the account, not merely observe a miraculous birth. Zachariah is presented first as a devoted servant who turns to God in difficulty, and the mercy shown to him becomes clear through the answer to his prayer.

phrases.translation: when he cried out to his Lord privately
phrases.explanation: Zachariah makes his supplication privately and softly, not to show off but with humility. The quiet manner highlights personal dependence on Allah and the sincerity of his request. The verse sets a tone of intimate prayer before revealing his words, showing that a person may bring a deep concern to God without seeking an audience or public recognition.

phrases.translation: saying, “My Lord! Surely my bones have become brittle, and grey hair has spread across my head, but I have never been disappointed in my prayer to You, my Lord
phrases.explanation: Zachariah describes his physical weakness through brittle bones and grey hair, then recalls that he has never been disappointed in praying to Allah. His words are not a complaint against God. They express age and need while grounding hope in past generosity, making his request a continuation of trust rather than a demand.

phrases.translation: And I am concerned about ˹the faith of˺ my relatives after me, since my wife is barren.
phrases.explanation: Zachariah worries about what will happen to his relatives after him and explains that his wife cannot bear a child. The concern is not only for his household. He fears what may become of the religious legacy entrusted to his family. The verse lets readers hear the vulnerability behind his prayer before he asks for an heir.

phrases.translation: So grant me, by Your grace, an heir
phrases.explanation: He asks Allah to grant him an heir through divine grace. The request is made despite the couple's circumstances, which appear to leave no ordinary path to a child. Zachariah is not claiming that he deserves an answer. He asks for a gift from God, trusting that mercy can reach beyond what human expectation considers possible.

phrases.translation: who will inherit ˹prophethood˺ from me and the family of Jacob,
phrases.explanation: Zachariah asks for a successor who will inherit from him and from the family of Jacob. The translation identifies this inheritance with prophethood, placing the request in the context of continuing guidance rather than ordinary wealth. He hopes that the responsibility of serving God will continue through someone who follows the prophetic family.

phrases.translation: and make him, O Lord, pleasing ˹to You˺!”
phrases.explanation: He asks that the child be pleasing to Allah. The request is not simply for a son or a successor, but for someone whose character and devotion make him worthy of God's approval. This completes the prayer with its true aim: Zachariah wants a family blessing that serves faith and goodness, not merely a personal comfort.

phrases.translation: ˹The angels announced,˺ “O Zachariah! Indeed, We give you the good news of ˹the birth of˺ a son, whose name will be John—a name We have not given to anyone before.”
phrases.explanation: The angels announce the birth of John and give his name before he is born. The name is described as unprecedented, underscoring the special nature of this gift. The announcement answers Zachariah's prayer with certainty, even though the circumstances he described seemed impossible. Allah's promise reaches beyond ordinary expectation and brings joy to the faithful.

phrases.translation: He wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren, and I have become extremely old?”
phrases.explanation: Zachariah is amazed and asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is extremely old. His question expresses wonder at the promise, not rejection of Allah's power. The verse allows the reader to recognize the natural obstacles he sees, setting up the answer that God's creative power is not limited by them.

phrases.translation: An angel replied, “So will it be! Your Lord says, ‘It is easy for Me, just as I created you before, when you were nothing!’”
phrases.explanation: The angel replies that the promise will come to pass because creating a child is easy for Allah. Zachariah himself was brought into existence when he had been nothing, so his own life is already a sign of divine creative power. The answer shifts his attention from physical impossibility to the Creator who gives existence.

phrases.translation: Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.”
phrases.explanation: Zachariah asks Allah for a sign confirming the good news. His request follows an announcement that astonished him, and the sign is granted as reassurance rather than as a condition he places on God's promise. The exchange shows that he continues turning to Allah as the source of both the promise and his certainty.

phrases.translation: He responded, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three nights, despite being healthy.”
phrases.explanation: His sign is that he will be unable to speak to people for three nights despite being healthy. The temporary silence is an extraordinary confirmation, not the result of illness. It also prepares for his later gesture to the people, when he communicates without speech and directs them to glorify Allah.

phrases.translation: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary, signalling to them to glorify ˹Allah˺ morning and evening
phrases.explanation: Zachariah leaves the sanctuary unable to speak and signals to his people to glorify Allah morning and evening. His gestures confirm the sign while continuing his devotion. The verse portrays worship as something he encourages even in silence, and shows that a limitation in speech need not prevent a person from directing others toward remembrance of God.

phrases.translation: ˹It was later said,˺ “O John! Hold firmly to the Scriptures.”
phrases.explanation: John is commanded to take the Scriptures firmly, with seriousness and diligence. The instruction asks him to hold to revelation rather than treat it as a passing lesson. The verse depicts religious learning as a responsibility requiring commitment, and prepares for the qualities that follow in the description of John's character.

phrases.translation: And We granted him wisdom while ˹he was still˺ a child
phrases.explanation: Allah grants John wisdom while he is still a child. His young age does not prevent him from receiving understanding and sound judgment from God. The verse presents wisdom as a gift, not simply the result of growing old, and shows that a young person can be entrusted with serious religious responsibility.

phrases.translation: as well as purity and compassion from Us. And he was God-fearing
phrases.explanation: John is given purity and compassion from Allah and is described as God-fearing. The qualities belong together: spiritual cleanliness is joined to mercy toward others and awareness of accountability before God. The verse presents his character as a divine blessing, rather than a reputation he built through pride or a claim he made for himself.

phrases.translation: and kind to his parents. He was neither arrogant nor disobedient
phrases.explanation: John is kind and dutiful toward his parents, without arrogance or disobedience. His devotion to Allah appears alongside care for his family, showing that religious goodness shapes ordinary relationships. The verse contrasts humility with self-importance and presents respect for one's parents as part of the admirable character granted to John.

phrases.translation: Peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day of his death, and the day he will be raised back to life
phrases.explanation: Peace and safety are declared for John at birth, at death, and when he is raised to life. These are the most vulnerable and decisive stages of a person's existence. The verse honors him with divine protection across them and points beyond his earthly life to resurrection, when every person returns to face what comes next.

phrases.translation: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Mary when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to recall Mary's story and her withdrawal from her family to a place in the east. Her separation prepares for a private and extraordinary event. The verse introduces Mary with dignity, placing her in a setting apart from her relatives before the angel's appearance changes the course of her life.

phrases.translation: screening herself off from them.
phrases.explanation: Mary puts a screen between herself and her family, seeking privacy in her retreat. The wording focuses on her separation from them, not on any wrongdoing. Her private place becomes the setting for a test she did not expect, showing how an ordinary act of seclusion can be followed by a moment of divine intervention.

phrases.translation: Then We sent to her Our angel, ˹Gabriel,˺ appearing before her as a man, perfectly formed
phrases.explanation: Allah sends an angel who appears to Mary in the form of a well-proportioned man. His human appearance explains her alarm in the next verse. The account describes how the messenger looked to her, while making clear that he was sent by God and not an ordinary visitor who had entered her private space.

phrases.translation: She appealed, “I truly seek refuge in the Most Compassionate from you! ˹So leave me alone˺ if you are God-fearing.”
phrases.explanation: Mary seeks refuge in the Most Compassionate and warns the stranger to leave if he fears God. Her response shows modesty and a desire for protection when she believes an unknown man has approached her. The verse presents her appeal as an act of faith, trusting Allah to guard her in a frightening and unexpected situation.

phrases.translation: He responded, “I am only a messenger from your Lord, ˹sent˺ to bless you with a pure son.”
phrases.explanation: The visitor identifies himself as a messenger from Mary's Lord and announces that she will have a pure son. His answer corrects her fear by explaining why he has come. The child is described as pure, and the message comes from God, not from any human relationship that Mary could have expected.

phrases.translation: She wondered, “How can I have a son when no man has ever touched me, nor am I unchaste?”
phrases.explanation: Mary asks how she could have a son when no man has touched her and she has not been unchaste. Her question affirms both her virginity and her moral innocence. She is not denying God's power. She is asking how the announced event can occur without the ordinary cause of conception.

phrases.translation: He replied, “So will it be! Your Lord says, ‘It is easy for Me.
phrases.explanation: The messenger repeats that the birth is easy for Allah. Mary's circumstances do not limit the Creator, just as old age and barrenness did not prevent the promised birth of John. The verse invites the reader to understand the event as a direct act of divine power rather than to seek an ordinary explanation for it.

phrases.translation: And so will We make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us.’
phrases.explanation: The child will be a sign for humanity and a mercy from Allah. His unusual birth will direct people to God's power, while his life and message will bring guidance. The verse gives the child's purpose in relation to humanity, not merely the wonder of how he was conceived.

phrases.translation: It is a matter ˹already˺ decreed.”
phrases.explanation: The matter is already decreed, so it will happen as Allah has willed. The statement ends Mary's uncertainty about whether the promise will be fulfilled. The story presents the birth as God's decision, not an event dependent on Mary's ability to explain or control the means by which it occurs.

phrases.translation: So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place
phrases.explanation: Mary conceives the child and withdraws with him to a remote place. The verse moves quickly from the announcement to the reality of pregnancy and seclusion. It does not describe the mechanics of the conception, but presents it as part of the sign Allah has decreed and shows Mary facing the event away from her family.

phrases.translation: Then the pains of labour drove her to the trunk of a palm tree.
phrases.explanation: The pains of labor drive Mary to the trunk of a palm tree. The line places her alone in the midst of childbirth, when her body is under strain and no human support is described. The location also prepares for the provision and reassurance that arrive in the following verses.

phrases.translation: She cried, “Alas! I wish I had died before this, and was a thing long forgotten!”
phrases.explanation: Mary cries that she wishes she had died before this and become something forgotten. Her words reveal anguish and fear about facing the event and the judgment of her people. The verse records her distress honestly rather than hiding it, before the voice comforts her and Allah provides food and water.

phrases.translation: So a voice reassured her from below her, “Do not grieve! Your Lord has provided a stream at your feet
phrases.explanation: A voice reassures Mary not to grieve and tells her that Allah has provided a stream at her feet. The source of the voice is discussed in different reports, so the verse's wording need not be used to claim more than it says. Its clear message is comfort and an immediate provision during labor.

phrases.translation: And shake the trunk of this palm tree towards you, it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you
phrases.explanation: Mary is instructed to shake the palm tree so ripe dates will fall for her. The command gives her a practical action to take even as Allah provides the fruit. The verse joins reliance on God with effort, and offers her food at a moment of exhaustion and vulnerability.

phrases.translation: So eat and drink, and put your heart at ease.
phrases.explanation: Mary is told to eat and drink from the provisions Allah has placed near her and to be comforted. Food and water answer her immediate physical need, while the instruction not to grieve addresses her fear. The verse shows care for both bodily distress and inner anguish after childbirth.

phrases.translation: But if you see any of the people, say, ‘I have vowed silence to the Most Compassionate, so I am not talking to anyone today.’”
phrases.explanation: If Mary meets anyone, she is to say that she has vowed silence to the Most Compassionate and will not speak that day. The vow explains why she will not defend herself in conversation. Instead, the infant will speak, making the event a sign that answers the accusations awaiting her.

phrases.translation: Then she returned to her people, carrying him.
phrases.explanation: Mary returns after the birth, carrying the child as she has been instructed. The verse moves from her private seclusion into public view, where the people will see circumstances they cannot explain. Her return places her before family and community without first giving her a chance to establish the story in words.

phrases.translation: They said ˹in shock˺, “O Mary! You have certainly done a horrible thing
phrases.explanation: The people react with shock and accuse Mary of a terrible act. The verse reports their response before they know what has happened, setting up the miraculous reply that follows. Their certainty should not be mistaken for truth: the chapter has already affirmed Mary's purity and the angel's promise of a son from Allah.

phrases.translation: O sister of Aaron! Your father was not an indecent man, nor was your mother unchaste.”
phrases.explanation: The people call Mary the sister of Aaron and point to the reputations of her parents. The phrase expresses their shock by comparing her with a family known to them for piety, though reports differ about the exact relationship meant by the title. Their words show the pressure of public suspicion and the demand that she answer for herself.

phrases.translation: So she pointed to the baby.
phrases.explanation: Mary points to the infant rather than answering with her own speech, following the instruction to remain silent. Her gesture directs the people toward the one who can answer the accusation. The verse shows her relying on the sign Allah has prepared instead of entering a dispute she had been told not to engage in.

phrases.translation: They exclaimed, “How can we talk to someone who is an infant in the cradle?”
phrases.explanation: The people are astonished that Mary directs them to a baby and ask how they can speak with someone in a cradle. Their question makes the next event extraordinary: the infant is about to address them. The verse shows that their challenge is understandable from ordinary experience, but this moment will exceed what they expect.

phrases.translation: ˹Jesus˺ declared, “I am truly a servant of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Jesus begins by identifying himself as a servant of Allah. This first declaration establishes his relation to God and rejects treating him as divine. In the moment of accusation against Mary, his words defend her by showing that the child is under God's care and has a message to deliver.

phrases.translation: He has destined me to be given the Scripture and to be a prophet
phrases.explanation: Jesus says that Allah has destined him to receive Scripture and to be a prophet. His future role is assigned by God before he can grow into it, making the infant's speech a sign of divine power. The statement identifies him as a recipient and messenger of revelation, not as the source of his own authority.

phrases.translation: He has made me a blessing wherever I go,
phrases.explanation: Jesus says Allah has made him a blessing wherever he goes. The commentators explain blessing as bringing benefit, though the precise forms of that benefit may vary. The phrase presents his life as a source of good for others, with that quality granted by God rather than earned through worldly power.

phrases.translation: and bid me to establish prayer and give alms-tax as long as I live
phrases.explanation: Jesus is commanded to establish prayer and give alms for as long as he lives. These acts connect his prophetic role to worship and responsibility toward others. The verse shows that even one honored with a miraculous birth remains a servant who worships Allah and carries out obligations throughout life.

phrases.translation: and to be kind to my mother.
phrases.explanation: Jesus says he is to be kind to his mother. His first words publicly vindicate Mary and then affirm a lasting duty of care toward her. The verse places honor for a parent within a life of worship, showing that gratitude and gentleness at home belong alongside public religious responsibility.

phrases.translation: He has not made me arrogant or defiant
phrases.explanation: Jesus says Allah has not made him arrogant or defiant. His description contrasts humility with the pride that rejects guidance and disobeys God. The verse gives a picture of prophetic character from the beginning of his speech, and frames his mission as service marked by obedience rather than self-exaltation.

phrases.translation: Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I will be raised back to life!”
phrases.explanation: Jesus declares peace upon himself at birth, death, and resurrection. The three moments mark the stages at which human beings are most vulnerable and accountable. His words echo the peace declared for John earlier in the chapter, while affirming that Jesus too remains a servant whose life and return are under Allah's protection.

phrases.translation: That is Jesus, son of Mary.
phrases.explanation: The verse identifies Jesus through his mother, Mary, and states his human lineage plainly. The direct naming counters claims that make him more than a servant. It also returns the reader to the miraculous birth narrative, where Jesus' own first words established his service to Allah.

phrases.translation: ˹And this is˺ a word of truth, about which they dispute
phrases.explanation: The account is described as true amid disagreement about Jesus. The verse asks readers to evaluate competing claims by the revelation's account rather than by speculation or inherited argument. Its conclusion prepares for the following clarification that Allah does not have a son and creates by command.

phrases.translation: It is not for Allah to take a son! Glory be to Him.
phrases.explanation: Allah is far above having a son. The verse rejects the idea that God belongs to a family of created beings or needs offspring. Its declaration of God's perfection corrects claims made about Jesus and protects the distinction between the Creator and every servant brought into existence.

phrases.translation: When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, “Be!” And it is
phrases.explanation: When Allah decrees something, He only says, “Be,” and it comes to be. The birth of Jesus is therefore a sign of God's command, not evidence that Jesus shares God's nature. The verse points to effortless creation and shows that divine power does not require a child or any other partner.

phrases.translation: ˹Jesus also declared,˺ “Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.”
phrases.explanation: Jesus calls Allah his Lord and the Lord of those addressed, then commands them to worship Him alone. The statement places Jesus among those who worship God, not above Him. The Straight Path is thus defined by devotion to the one Lord, a message shared by the prophets described throughout this chapter.

phrases.translation: Yet their ˹various˺ groups have differed among themselves ˹about him˺, so woe to the disbelievers when they face a tremendous Day
phrases.explanation: Groups disagree about Jesus, and the verse warns of a tremendous Day for those who reject the truth. The text acknowledges division without treating every claim as equally sound. Its warning turns attention from the arguments of this world to the day when the consequences of disbelief will become clear.

phrases.translation: How clearly will they hear and see on the Day they will come to Us!
phrases.explanation: On the Day people come before Allah, their hearing and sight will be clear and complete. They will perceive the truth they ignored in worldly life. The verse describes a future awakening in contrast with present heedlessness, when evidence is no longer hidden and excuses cannot keep people from seeing their condition.

phrases.translation: But today the wrongdoers are clearly astray
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers are already clearly astray in this life, even if they do not recognize it. The contrast with the clarity of Judgment Day urges people to respond before that day arrives. Guidance is available now, while the full consequences of rejecting it will only become unmistakable when they stand before Allah.

phrases.translation: And warn them ˹O Prophet˺ of the Day of Regret,
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to warn people about the Day of Regret. On that day, those who neglected faith will grieve over what they failed to do and over the outcome they could have avoided. The warning is meant for people still able to respond, not merely to describe sorrow after the chance to change has passed.

phrases.translation: when all matters will be settled, while they are ˹engrossed˺ in heedlessness and disbelief
phrases.explanation: All matters will be settled, while people in worldly life remain heedless and disbelieving. The verse contrasts the finality of judgment with the distraction of the present. It calls listeners to take the message seriously now, because decisions that seem distant will be resolved and exposed when the promised Day comes.

phrases.translation: Indeed, it is We Who will succeed the earth and whoever is on it. And to Us they will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation: Allah will remain when the earth and everyone on it have passed away, and all creation will return to Him. The verse reassures the Prophet not to be overcome by rejection, since every person will ultimately face God. It also reminds the listener that possessions and power are temporary, while accountability to Allah is certain.

phrases.translation: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Abraham. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet
phrases.explanation: Abraham is introduced as a truthful man and a prophet. His account follows the declaration that all people return to Allah, offering an example of someone who speaks honestly even when addressing his own father. The description establishes his integrity before the story shows the courage and respect with which he calls his family to worship God.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his father, “O dear father! Why do you worship what can neither hear nor see, nor benefit you at all
phrases.explanation: Abraham asks his father why he worships idols that cannot hear, see, or bring benefit. His question exposes the gap between the respect people give an object and its inability to respond or help. He begins with a gentle appeal, inviting his father to reflect rather than opening with insult or force.

phrases.translation: O dear father! I have certainly received some knowledge which you have not received, so follow me and I will guide you to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Abraham says he has received knowledge that his father has not and invites him to follow so he can guide him to the Straight Path. The claim is a respectful offer of counsel, not a boast about personal superiority. He wants his father to benefit from revelation and find a way directed by Allah.

phrases.translation: O dear father! Do not worship Satan. Surely Satan is ever rebellious against the Most Compassionate
phrases.explanation: Abraham warns his father not to worship Satan, describing Satan as persistently rebellious against the Most Compassionate. Worship of idols is linked to following the one who calls people away from God. The appeal remains personal and respectful, but it makes clear that false worship has a spiritual source and leads away from mercy.

phrases.translation: O dear father! I truly fear that you will be touched by a torment from the Most Compassionate, and become Satan’s companion ˹in Hell˺.”
phrases.explanation: Abraham fears that his father may face punishment from the Most Compassionate and become an ally of Satan. His warning comes from concern for his father's fate, not a desire to humiliate him. The verse presents fear of accountability as part of sincere advice, especially when the person being warned is someone deeply loved.

phrases.translation: He threatened, “How dare you reject my idols, O Abraham! If you do not desist, I will certainly stone you ˹to death˺.
phrases.explanation: Abraham's father responds with a threat of violence if he continues rejecting the idols. The sharp change from Abraham's gentle appeal shows the danger he faces for speaking against inherited worship. The verse records the father's hostility without endorsing it, and makes the choice between truth and family pressure painfully clear.

phrases.translation: So be gone from me for a long time!”
phrases.explanation: The father orders Abraham to leave for a long time. His rejection separates them, but it does not make Abraham answer with violence or abuse. The exchange shows that family ties can be tested by religious disagreement, while the believer remains responsible for responding with restraint even when treated harshly.

phrases.translation: Abraham responded, “Peace be upon you! I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness.
phrases.explanation: Abraham answers his father's threat with a promise of peace and says he will ask Allah to forgive him. His response maintains respect without surrendering his belief. The verse presents patience under insult as a deliberate choice and shows that Abraham continues to hope for his father's guidance after being rejected.

phrases.translation: He has truly been Most Gracious to me
phrases.explanation: Abraham says that Allah has been gracious to him. Gratitude helps him endure separation and hostility without turning away from his Lord. The statement also recalls the mercy described at the start of the chapter: Allah cares for His servants, and that care gives Abraham confidence as he faces an uncertain future.

phrases.translation: As I distance myself from ˹all of˺ you and from whatever you invoke besides Allah,
phrases.explanation: Abraham decides to withdraw from his people and the idols they invoke besides Allah. His departure follows the father's threat and the community's continued worship of idols. The verse portrays separation as a consequence of refusing false worship, while the next words show that Abraham does not abandon prayer when he leaves his family.

phrases.translation: I will ˹continue to˺ call upon my Lord ˹alone˺, trusting that I will never be disappointed in invoking my Lord.”
phrases.explanation: He will continue to call upon his Lord, confident that his prayer will not be fruitless. Abraham replaces the idols and rejected relationships with reliance on Allah. The verse teaches that hardship and isolation need not end a person's hope, because the Lord who hears supplication is not limited by the loss of human support.

phrases.translation: So after he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made each of them a prophet
phrases.explanation: After Abraham leaves his people and their idols, Allah grants him Isaac and Jacob, and makes both prophets. The answer to his separation is not simply new family ties, but a line of prophetic guidance. The verse shows that leaving wrongdoing for Allah's sake can be followed by blessings that support faith across generations.

phrases.translation: We showered them with Our mercy,
phrases.explanation: Allah bestows mercy upon Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The gift answers the hardship of Abraham's departure and includes the family and guidance he had hoped for. The verse presents their blessings as coming from God, not as a reward they could claim by ancestry alone.

phrases.translation: and blessed them with honourable mention
phrases.explanation: The family is also given an honorable mention. Their names remain connected with truth and devotion long after their lives, making their example a continuing blessing for later people. The verse pairs divine mercy with a good reputation, showing how faithfulness can leave a legacy that outlasts wealth and worldly status.

phrases.translation: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Moses. He was truly a chosen man, and was a messenger and a prophet
phrases.explanation: Moses is introduced as a chosen man, a messenger, and a prophet. The verse directs the Prophet to remember and recount his story, continuing the chapter's examples of people who received revelation. Moses' selection and mission come from Allah, and the following verses describe how God honored and supported him.

phrases.translation: We called him from the right side of Mount Ṭûr, and drew him near, speaking ˹with him˺ directly
phrases.explanation: Allah calls Moses from the side of Mount Tur and draws him near to speak with him directly. The verse describes a special encounter and a particular honor granted to Moses. It emphasizes that revelation comes from God, while leaving the exact manner of that speech beyond what the wording explains.

phrases.translation: And We appointed for him—out of Our grace—his brother, Aaron, as a prophet
phrases.explanation: Out of mercy, Allah gives Moses his brother Aaron as a prophet. Aaron's prophethood strengthens Moses' mission and provides him with support. The verse presents companionship in service to God as a blessing, and shows that divine help may include another person who shares the responsibility of delivering guidance.

phrases.translation: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Ishmael. He was truly a man of his word, and was a messenger and a prophet
phrases.explanation: Ishmael is remembered as a man who kept his word and as a messenger and prophet. His reliability is highlighted alongside his prophetic role, showing that trustworthiness is part of religious excellence. The verse presents his character as an example and continues the chapter's account of servants whom Allah chose for guidance.

phrases.translation: He used to urge his people to pray and give alms-tax. And his Lord was well pleased with him
phrases.explanation: Ishmael urged his household to pray and give alms, and Allah was pleased with him. His care for his family included guiding them toward worship and generosity. The verse links the prophet's private responsibilities with his public faith, showing that religious leadership begins with practicing and encouraging what is good among one's own people.

phrases.translation: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Enoch. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet
phrases.explanation: Enoch is described as a truthful man and a prophet. The verse again connects honesty with receiving revelation, presenting truthfulness as a defining quality of those chosen to guide others. His brief mention alongside Moses and Ishmael shows that many prophets served Allah, even when the text does not recount their full stories.

phrases.translation: And We elevated him to an honourable status
phrases.explanation: Enoch is said to have been raised to an honorable status. Reports differ about the specific place meant, but the verse's clear point is that Allah gave him distinction and a lofty rank. The statement honors him without requiring readers to settle details that the revelation does not spell out here.

phrases.translation: Those were ˹some of˺ the prophets who Allah has blessed from among the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those We ˹rightly˺ guided and chose.
phrases.explanation: The prophets named in the chapter come from several generations and families, yet they share Allah's favor and guidance. The verse gathers them into one line of divine care, including descendants of Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Israel. Their varied histories point to a common source of prophethood and a shared call to worship God.

phrases.translation: Whenever the revelations of the Most Compassionate were recited to them, they fell down, prostrating and weeping
phrases.explanation: When these chosen servants hear revelations from the Most Compassionate, they fall in prostration and weep. Their response is humble worship, not pride in their rank. The verse presents tears and prostration as signs of receptive hearts, showing that revelation moved the prophets toward devotion rather than merely giving them status among people.

phrases.translation: But they were succeeded by generations who neglected prayer and followed their lusts
phrases.explanation: Later generations neglect prayer and follow their desires, turning away from the example of the prophets. The verse treats both failures together: abandoning worship and allowing appetite to govern conduct. It warns that a community can lose its way when it no longer maintains devotion to Allah or restrains itself according to His guidance.

phrases.translation: and so will soon face the evil consequences
phrases.explanation: Those who follow this path will face its evil consequences. The warning is serious, but the next verse immediately leaves a door open for repentance, faith, and good deeds. The passage therefore calls people to change before the outcome arrives, rather than declaring every person who has failed in the past beyond hope.

phrases.translation: As for those who repent, believe, and do good, it is they who will be admitted into Paradise, never being denied any reward
phrases.explanation: People who repent, believe, and do good are promised entry into Paradise without having their reward reduced. The verse answers the warning about neglect with a clear path back. Repentance means turning from wrongdoing toward Allah, while faith and righteous action show that the return is sincere and not merely a claim.

phrases.translation: ˹They will be in˺ the Gardens of Eternity, promised in trust by the Most Compassionate to His servants. Surely His promise will be fulfilled
phrases.explanation: The repentant believers will enter Gardens of Eternity, promised by the Most Compassionate to His servants. The promise is described as trustworthy and certain to be fulfilled. The verse balances the earlier warning with hope, showing that Allah's mercy and the lasting reward of Paradise remain open to those who return to Him.

phrases.translation: There they will never hear any idle talk—only ˹greetings of˺ peace.
phrases.explanation: In Paradise, people will hear no idle or false talk, only greetings of peace. The description contrasts the confusion and harm of worldly speech with a home where safety and goodwill prevail. Peace is not a passing greeting there, but the sound that replaces speech that distracts, insults, or troubles people.

phrases.translation: And there they will have their provisions morning and evening
phrases.explanation: The people of Paradise will receive their provisions morning and evening. The wording conveys continual care and provision, not anxiety about scarcity. The verse describes a life of comfort and honor in which their needs are met, completing the picture of peace with the assurance of sustenance from Allah.

phrases.translation: That is Paradise, which We will grant to whoever is devout among Our servants
phrases.explanation: This is the Paradise promised to whoever among Allah's servants is devout. The verse gathers the previous descriptions into a direct assurance and identifies the people for whom the promise is made. Devotion means living with awareness of God and avoiding what He forbids, not simply wishing for the reward without following His guidance.

phrases.translation: “We only descend by the command of your Lord.
phrases.explanation: The angels say that they descend only by the command of the Lord. Their coming is not governed by their own choice or by a human demand. The statement answers the concern behind their absence and places revelation and every angelic mission under Allah's authority.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever is before us, and whatever is behind us, and everything in between. And your Lord is never forgetful
phrases.explanation: Everything before, behind, and between belongs to Allah, and He is never forgetful. The language encompasses all times and places, affirming that nothing lies outside God's knowledge or care. The verse reassures the Prophet that a delay in angelic revelation does not mean Allah has forgotten him or abandoned His promise.

phrases.translation: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the heavens, and the earth, and everything in between.
phrases.explanation: Allah is the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. His authority is not limited to one place or part of creation. The description grounds the command that follows: because He governs everything, worship belongs to Him alone and no rival shares His lordship.

phrases.translation: So worship Him ˹alone˺, and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of anyone equal to Him ˹in His attributes˺?”
phrases.explanation: People are commanded to worship Allah alone and remain steadfast in that worship. The question asks whether anyone is truly equal to Him in the qualities that belong to God. The verse moves from describing the Lord to the response owed to Him: sustained devotion, with no created being treated as His equal.

phrases.translation: Yet ˹some˺ people ask ˹mockingly˺, “After I die, will I really be raised to life again?”
phrases.explanation: Some people ask mockingly whether they will really be raised after death. Their question dismisses resurrection as absurd, even though their own existence began when they were nothing. The verse exposes their refusal to take the promise seriously and prepares the answer that follows by challenging them to remember how life began.

phrases.translation: Do ˹such˺ people not remember that We created them before, when they were nothing
phrases.explanation: People are asked whether they remember that Allah created them before, when they did not exist. The first creation is evidence that bringing people back is within God's power. The verse answers denial of resurrection with a simple reminder of human origins, turning the question back on those who imagine that death makes them beyond the Creator's reach.

phrases.translation: By your Lord ˹O Prophet˺! We will surely gather them along with the devils, and then set them around Hell on their knees
phrases.explanation: Allah swears by the Prophet's Lord that the rejecters will be gathered with the devils and brought around Hell on their knees. The scene shows the seriousness of the judgment they mocked. No one can avoid being gathered, and the verse pictures humiliation before it describes how the most defiant among them will be singled out.

phrases.translation: Then We will certainly begin by dragging out of every group the ones most defiant to the Most Compassionate
phrases.explanation: From every group, Allah will bring forward those most defiant toward the Most Compassionate. The verse describes a judgment that exposes the strongest opposition, not a random selection. Their prominence in wrongdoing will not protect them. Instead, it makes their responsibility plain when they are called to answer before God.

phrases.translation: And We truly know best who is most deserving of burning in it
phrases.explanation: Allah knows best who is most deserving of the Fire. Human beings may judge by outward status or argue over who is worst, but God's knowledge reaches every hidden intention and deed. The verse affirms that the final judgment belongs to Allah, who cannot be misled about anyone's true responsibility.

phrases.translation: There is none of you who will not pass over it. ˹This is˺ a decree your Lord must fulfil
phrases.explanation: Every person will come to or pass over Hell, as Allah has decreed. The exact nature of this passage is discussed in the commentary, while the next verse makes clear that the devout are delivered and wrongdoers remain. The warning applies to all people, but it does not say that everyone has the same final outcome.

phrases.translation: Then We will deliver those who were devout, leaving the wrongdoers there on their knees
phrases.explanation: Allah delivers those who were devout and leaves the wrongdoers in Hell on their knees. The verse clarifies the outcome after the universal passage mentioned before it. The devout are not saved by status or ancestry, but by their relation to Allah, while those who persisted in wrongdoing face the consequence of their choices.

phrases.translation: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, the disbelievers ask the believers ˹mockingly˺, “Which of the two of us is better in status and superior in assembly?”
phrases.explanation: When revelation is recited, disbelievers mock believers by comparing their worldly status and gathering. They assume that wealth, influence, and a large assembly prove that their beliefs are better. The verse exposes this as a shallow measure of truth and prepares the reminder that prosperous communities before them were also destroyed.

phrases.translation: ˹Imagine, O Prophet˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them, who were far better in luxury and splendour
phrases.explanation: Many earlier peoples had more luxury and a more impressive appearance than the present deniers, yet they were destroyed. Material comfort therefore cannot prove that a group is favored or secure. The verse answers the boast in the previous line by reminding people that worldly display has never protected a community from judgment.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whoever is ˹entrenched˺ in misguidance, the Most Compassionate will allow them plenty of time,
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to say that people entrenched in misguidance may be given plenty of time by the Most Compassionate. A delay is not a declaration that their path is right or that judgment has been canceled. The verse explains why apparent worldly success can continue even while a person remains far from guidance.

phrases.translation: until—behold!—they face what they are threatened with: either the torment or the Hour. Only then will they realize who is worse in position and inferior in manpower.”
phrases.explanation: Eventually they will face the torment or the Hour and learn who is truly worse in position and weaker in support. The comparison reverses the worldly boast of the disbelievers. Their current advantage cannot decide the final judgment, and their allies will not protect them when the promised consequence arrives.

phrases.translation: And Allah increases in guidance those who are ˹rightly˺ guided.
phrases.explanation: Allah increases in guidance those who are already rightly guided. Responding to guidance brings further clarity and firmness, rather than leaving a person unchanged. The statement contrasts with persistent misguidance and encourages people to act on what they know, trusting Allah to increase the direction of those who sincerely follow it.

phrases.translation: And the everlasting good deeds are far better with your Lord in reward and in outcome
phrases.explanation: Everlasting good deeds are better with Allah in reward and in outcome than temporary status or possessions. The phrase returns to the lasting contrast running through the chapter: worldly advantages fade, while righteous acts endure. It invites people to invest their effort in what will benefit them when they stand before their Lord.

phrases.translation: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who rejects Our revelations yet boasts, “I will definitely be granted ˹plenty of˺ wealth and children ˹if there is an afterlife˺.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is asked to consider someone who rejects Allah's revelations yet confidently expects wealth and children if an afterlife exists. The man treats future prosperity as certain without evidence. The verse challenges this self-assurance, asking whether he has knowledge of the unseen or any promise from the Most Compassionate.

phrases.translation: Has he looked into the unseen or taken a pledge from the Most Compassionate
phrases.explanation: The question denies that the boastful person has seen the unseen or received a pledge from Allah. His confidence about future wealth and children rests on neither knowledge nor a divine promise. The verse exposes the emptiness of claiming a reward in the afterlife while rejecting the revelation that teaches people how to prepare for it.

phrases.translation: Not at all! We certainly record whatever he claims and will increase his punishment extensively
phrases.explanation: Allah rejects the man's claim and says that it will be recorded, with his punishment increased. The warning shows that speech can reveal a person's arrogance and false confidence, and that such claims are not forgotten. A person should not treat unsupported boasts as harmless when they deny accountability before God.

phrases.translation: And We will inherit what he boasts of, and he will come before Us all by himself
phrases.explanation: Allah will take away what the man boasts of, and he will come before Him alone. Wealth and children cannot accompany him as protectors or guarantee his hoped-for reward. The verse strips away the security he imagined and returns to a central theme of the chapter: each person stands individually before Allah.

phrases.translation: They have taken other gods, instead of Allah, seeking strength ˹and protection˺ through them
phrases.explanation: People take other gods besides Allah, hoping those gods will give them strength and protection. The verse exposes the motive behind worshipping them: they are treated as sources of security. But created things cannot provide what belongs to God, and reliance on them leaves people unprepared for the judgment described in the verses that follow.

phrases.translation: But no! Those ˹gods˺ will deny their worship and turn against them
phrases.explanation: The false gods will deny that their worshippers served them and will turn against them. Those who expected support will instead find that their chosen objects of devotion cannot help them. The verse overturns the hope expressed before it, showing that partners invoked besides Allah will not share divine authority or protect their followers.

phrases.translation: Do you ˹O Prophet˺ not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, constantly inciting them
phrases.explanation: Allah describes the devils as continually inciting the disbelievers. Their influence stirs people toward wrongdoing and misguidance, but the verse does not make them an excuse that removes human responsibility. The warning explains the pressure toward rejection and prepares the Prophet not to demand immediate punishment for those who persist.

phrases.translation: So do not be in haste against them, for indeed We are ˹closely˺ counting down their days
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to hurry the punishment of the disbelievers, because Allah is counting their days. The delay is measured and purposeful, not forgetfulness or approval. The verse asks the messenger to leave the timing to God, whose knowledge includes every person's remaining life and the appointed moment of judgment.

phrases.translation: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather the righteous before the Most Compassionate as an honoured delegation
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection, the devout are gathered before the Most Compassionate as an honored delegation. The image portrays welcome and dignity for those who feared God and obeyed Him. It contrasts their reception with the fate of wrongdoers in the next verse, showing how different responses to guidance lead to different endings.

phrases.translation: and drive the wicked to Hell like a thirsty herd
phrases.explanation: The wicked are driven to Hell thirsty, like a herd being taken to water. The image reverses the usual promise of a watering place: those who arrive at Hell do so in distress, not to be refreshed. The verse emphasizes the humiliation and need of people who rejected guidance, in contrast with the welcome given to the devout.

phrases.translation: None will have the right to intercede, except those who have taken a covenant from the Most Compassionate
phrases.explanation: No one possesses an independent right to intercede. The exception is only for those who have a covenant from the Most Compassionate, so any intercession remains under Allah's authority. The verse rejects the idea that a person's allies or claimed partners can guarantee rescue, and places hope in God's permission and promise.

phrases.translation: They say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring.”
phrases.explanation: The claim that the Most Compassionate has offspring is quoted before the verses reject it. The phrase identifies the belief being addressed without treating it as truth. Its placement recalls the chapter's earlier denial that Allah has a child, and prepares a vivid description of how grave this claim is.

phrases.translation: You have certainly made an outrageous claim
phrases.explanation: The claim is called outrageous and immense. The verse's force reflects the seriousness of attributing a child to Allah, which confuses the Creator with created beings. The warning is not aimed at a minor difference in wording. It confronts a claim about God's nature that the chapter has repeatedly rejected.

phrases.translation: by which the heavens are about to burst, the earth to split apart, and the mountains to crumble to pieces
phrases.explanation: The heavens are described as nearly bursting, the earth splitting, and the mountains crumbling because of this claim. The cosmic imagery conveys the magnitude of the offense against Allah. It should be read as a forceful expression of its seriousness, not as an invitation to calculate a physical event in the created world.

phrases.translation: in protest of attributing children to the Most Compassionate
phrases.explanation: The verse says that creation responds with horror to the claim that the Most Compassionate has a child. The heavens, earth, and mountains are presented as unable to bear such an attribution. The image reinforces the separation between the eternal Creator and the created world, which depends entirely on Him.

phrases.translation: It does not befit ˹the majesty of˺ the Most Compassionate to have children
phrases.explanation: It does not befit the Most Compassionate to have children. The verse rejects the claim at its root: Allah is not like created beings who depend on family or are subject to human needs. His greatness and mercy are not diminished by refusing to attribute to Him qualities that belong to creation.

phrases.translation: There is none in the heavens or the earth who will not return to the Most Compassionate in full submission
phrases.explanation: Everyone in the heavens and earth will return to the Most Compassionate as a servant. No angel, human being, or other creature stands outside God's authority. The verse replaces the idea of divine offspring with a universal truth: all creation belongs to Allah and will submit to Him.

phrases.translation: Indeed, He fully knows them and has counted them precisely
phrases.explanation: Allah knows every creature fully and has counted each one precisely. No person is lost in the multitude or hidden from His knowledge. The verse supports the certainty of individual judgment: because God knows every person and every deed, He can call each one to account without confusion or injustice.

phrases.translation: And each of them will return to Him on the Day of Judgment all alone
phrases.explanation: Every person will come before Allah alone on the Day of Judgment. No family, wealth, or companion can take another's place or shield them from their own account. The verse closes the argument about God's servants by reminding readers that all are His creatures and each will meet Him individually.

phrases.translation: As for those who believe and do good,
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do good are distinguished from the people who reject Allah's signs. Faith is joined to righteous action throughout this chapter, and this promise confirms that good deeds are not lost. The Most Compassionate responds to sincere belief with a lasting gift that cannot be secured through status or boasting.

phrases.translation: the Most Compassionate will ˹certainly˺ bless them with ˹genuine˺ love
phrases.explanation: Allah will place genuine love for the believers in the hearts of others. The verse presents this affection as a gift from the Most Compassionate, not something people can demand by seeking fame. A life of faith and goodness can leave a welcome legacy, while the final source of acceptance remains God's favor.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺
phrases.explanation: Allah has made the Qur'an easy in the Prophet's own language. This ease enables him to recite and convey the message clearly to his people. The verse presents the revelation as accessible guidance, while keeping its source divine rather than treating its familiar language as evidence that it is merely human speech.

phrases.translation: so with it you may give good news to the righteous and warn those who are contentious
phrases.explanation: The Qur'an gives good news to the righteous and warns people who are contentious. The same revelation offers hope to those who respond well and cautions those who persist in argument and rejection. Its purpose is not only to be recited, but to move listeners toward faith and away from the consequences of wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them! Do you ˹still˺ see any of them, or ˹even˺ hear from them the slightest sound
phrases.explanation: Many earlier generations were destroyed, and no trace or even faint sound remains from them. The final question challenges the present audience to learn from their absence. Their former power and visibility did not last, so people should not assume that current strength guarantees safety from judgment or makes Allah's warning irrelevant.
